The GrowthCred field guide

Working with GrowthCred, your first 30 days need a plan. A blind rollout wastes your cash.

Before you let anyone change how your business runs.

You should know what happens next. Here is how GrowthCred runs from application to your first monthly review.

Quick answer

The first result is due within 14 days of the deploy step starting. It's tested against real examples from your business.

3 min read

You'll learn

  1. How the application, scoping call, and audit map your bottlenecks before any build starts
  2. How a 14-day first result and a 30-day review keep work tied to real business rules

Why listen to GrowthCred

GrowthCred is a Johannesburg AI implementation and training company. I teach AI at Melsoft Academy. I helped build an isiZulu and English speech AI system. It was presented at Parliament in Cape Town.

1Before day one: skip blind pitches and scope your real bottleneck

The problem

  1. Cold pitches waste time before anyone knows how your business runs.
  2. Limited spots mean rushed builds fail when fit and scope are vague.

The way through

  1. Start with an application that shows where you are stuck.
  2. You use a working call to align on fit, scope, and cost together.

You start with a working scope, not a blind checkout.

2Step one: stop guessing and price the hours stuck on you

The problem

  1. Owners stay trapped in routine tasks that wait on their say-so.
  2. Unwritten rules leave builds guessing on pricing, promises, and tone.

The way through

  1. Audit where you are the bottleneck.
  2. Put a rand value on stuck hours. Write down your rules for pricing, promises, and how you talk.

Every system builds on your written rules, not guesswork.

3Step two: ditch slow demos. Ship a first result in 14 days for you

The problem

  1. Generic demos prove little when your real inputs and edge cases differ.
  2. Unchecked automation risks prices, promises, or external messages going wrong.

The way through

  1. Target your highest-value audit task first for a result within 14 days.
  2. Test on real examples with your team while people keep approval control.

People stay responsible for prices, commitments, and outward actions.

Apply

4Step three: stop one-off launches and track what moves in month one for you

The problem

  1. Live tools drift when business needs shift and nobody tracks results.
  2. Without a baseline, you cannot tell if the rollout actually helped. If the Command Core doesn't give you back at least 20% of your week, the engagement is on us.

The way through

  1. Track live systems monthly and add capabilities as needs change.
  2. End month one with a review measured against where you started.

Month one ends with a review measured against your starting baseline.
